headline: Learned models extend genetic association testing to imaging and disease progression
label: Deep Learning Genotype Phenotype Mapping
summary: Deep and multivariate models are now coupled to association testing, shifting them from prediction toward locus-level inference.
synthesis: The common thread is genetic association inference, in which learned or multivariate models localize genetic effects across heterogeneous phenotypes. A neural network trained on genome-wide genotypes uses post hoc interpretability scores to detect associated loci and estimate P-values, validated by simulation. RVGA applies representation learning to voxel-level GWAS, reducing compute and storage by over 200-fold while denoising images and estimating voxel heritability. ReverseGWAS identifies combinations of phenotypes associated with a genotype, while a probabilistic genetics-driven model flags SNPs with novel effects on Huntington's disease progression. A GxE method combines additive, dominant, and recessive tests via Cauchy p-value aggregation. What is new is coupling learned representations with association testing, moving deep models from prediction toward locus- and liability-level inference. The Y chromosome study adds germline and somatic regulatory evidence for type 2 diabetes.
